Member name fields (`first_name`, `last_name`, `middle_names`, `maiden_name`, `baptismal_name`, `academic_title`, etc.) are stored exactly as submitted, with no server-side trimming of leading/trailing whitespace. A member saved with a trailing/leading space (e.g. via copy-paste, or a stray keystroke in the member sheet) will not reliably match search:

- Global search: `member_name_search_clause` in `backend/app/services/member_search.py` does a plain `ilike("%query%")` against `first_name`/`last_name`/`maiden_name` — an untrimmed stored value still matches substrings fine, but any *typed* search query the user types with accidental leading/trailing space, or exact-match-style UI treatments elsewhere, can behave inconsistently. - Trim whitespace from name-like string fields server-side before insert/update (e.g. via a Pydantic `field_validator`/`model_validator` in the relevant schemas in `backend/app/schemas/family.py`, so it applies uniformly regardless of caller).

- Add trimming in the Pydantic schemas used for member create/update (`MemberCreate`/`MemberUpdate` and friends in `backend/app/schemas/family.py`), mirroring the trimming `gedcom.py` already does per-field.
